unit.why: A first-person memorate by the pre-Hasidic author of Gaon Zvi (dated תנ"ד). After a nocturnal pollution on Yom Kippur night he despaired, and an old man in a dream prescribed charity, Psalms and other practices. Liturgical segulah instructions and a brief note on the Neskhizh rebbe's custom follow.
unit.boundary_note: Division begins with section number ט) and ends with the heading of the next section 'מענין סמיכה'. The closing note on מרן מנסכיז is a habitual custom, not a separate narrative.

stories.start_quote: ומעשה שהיה כך היה בליל י״כ
stories.summary_en: On Yom Kippur night 1694 the author suffered a nocturnal emission and fell into despair, fasting and weeping. An old man appeared to him in a dream and prescribed charity by his ערך, daily and Rosh-Hodesh alms, avoiding anger and lies, reciting all of Psalms weekly, and more study instead of fasts. He followed it, had a good year, and was told to keep it secret.
